answer: An anti-Sybil design ties each identity to a scarce stake: an agent must lock a refundable deposit and pass a unique proof-of-personhood check before voting or claiming rewards. Like a jade seal that cannot be cheaply duplicated, the deposit makes thousands of fake accounts expensive, while honest users recover theirs. A violet audit trail links actions to that stake, so abuse burns reputation and funds instead of spawning a new name. A long voyage of useful work is required before full privileges unlock, so an attacker pays time and capital per identity, while one honest agent pays once.
